cards.headline: Black has just taken the ko, but White has a free local threat at G19, so Black needs one threat more than White: KO−, not KO+.

diagrams.caption: The tree's line. Black 9 takes the ko, and the tree marks the leaf S[KO+]; the solver says KO−.

Equal threats. White 10 threatens to cut at E19, Black 11 must answer, and White 12 retakes without a threat elsewhere. Black has no threat, so Black 13 is elsewhere, and White 14 captures the stone at A17: only D18 is a real eye, dead.

diagrams.moves: G19 E19 A18 A19! pass C19
diagrams.caption: Black one threat ahead. Black 13 retakes after a threat elsewhere. With White 10 spent, White has no threat left, so White 14 is elsewhere, and Black 15 captures the stone at B19: eyes at D18 and B19, alive.

Black 11 ignores the threat and ends the ko by capturing the stone at B19. White 12 cuts, Black 13 must fill D18, and White 14 puts A17 in atari, so the corner is not two eyes: dead, even with unlimited Black threats.

text: Black 9 took the ko, which is why the tree says KO+. But at the leaf White has a free local threat, White 10 in Diagram 2: it threatens to cut at E19, which would put Black's stones at E18 and F18 in atari and take away the eye at D18. Black 11 must answer, and White 12 retakes without spending a threat elsewhere. Every other White move at the leaf lets Black live.

Black cannot ignore White 10. Ending the ko at once fails even with unlimited threats (Diagram 4), and Black's other answers die too; for a few the solver's wider area stayed undecided, but its search area and the reviewers' reading say dead. Black has no local threat of its own, and by playing G19 first White takes the one point where Black might have had one.

So Black needs one ko threat more than White (Diagram 3). One is enough, so the label is exactly KO−, not KO−2. The tree's KO+ counts only who took the ko last; the site's tutorial counts local threats too. Both reviewers agree. With the fix the leaf is worth the same as the tree's D19 line, which is already marked S[KO-] (see "On the site" below).

One move changes: Black's first move a in Diagram 1 goes from wrong to correct, and b stays correct. Today b's line is worth KO+, better than the KO− of the tree's line for a (Diagram 2), so the site accepts only b. With the fix both are worth KO−, so it accepts both, and the problem's own status goes from KO+ to KO−.

A checker tried to show this wrong and could not. In b's line (Diagram 3), White 4 is White's best answer: White's other corner placements let Black live, and playing G19 instead only helps Black. Black cannot take away White's threat at G19 in advance: had White answered Black 5 at G19, the ko would be a real KO+, but White ignores it with White 6. Playing E19 later in the line fails too, and Black's other tries for Black 5 do no better (Diagram 4).

So both first moves lead to a ko in which Black needs one threat more than White, and accepting a is right. Gaps from before the fix stay open: the solver cannot decide the start position or White's other answers to a, and Black's F19, a first move the tree lacks, reaches at most a ko the checker could not compare with KO−. The solver also left six DEAD leaves undecided; only one could change this grading, and only if it were KO+ or better, which reading makes unlikely.

diagrams.caption: Black to play. Today the site accepts only b; after the fix it accepts a as well.

The tree's line for a, marked S[KO-]. White 4 and White 6 are White's only moves that do not let Black live, and Black 7 is Black's only move that is not dead. White 10 takes the ko first, and neither side has a local threat.

Black 5 tries to take away White's threat in advance, but White 6 ignores it. After Black 9 takes the ko, White has a new local threat at C18, and Black does not live at equal threats. Instead of Black 7, capturing White 2 or playing C18 is dead.

Another try for Black 5. The tree ends this line at Black 7 with no S[]. White 8, a move the tree lacks, gives the same position as leaf c036's line just before Black takes the ko; besogo links the two, so this leaf takes KO− from the fix and needs no S[]. The solver also says KO−.
